summary: This image presents a violin plot comparing feedback questionnaire results for two groups: template-based and LLM-based. The plot illustrates the distribution and mean scores of responses on a Likert scale from 1 to 7 for various questions. Key findings include: 'Did questions help in the selection of unviable goals?' (p-value = 0.34), 'Did questions help to improve a plan?' (p-value = 0.01), 'Did the possibility to ask questions reduce the level of difficulty?' (p-value = 0.02), 'Did the possibility to ask questions help?' (p-value = 0.07), 'How confident are you that you know which plans are possible?' (p-value = 0.67), 'How satisfied are you with your task?' (p-value = 0.51), and 'How easy was the task for you?' (p-value = 0.26). The LLM-based approach significantly outperforms the template-based method in assisting participants with their plans and reducing difficulty.
